title: LCI routing_table on-link fe80::/10 drops zone_id
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/client/addressing.py LciAddressAssignment.routing_table() always returns LciRoute(prefix=fe80::/10, via=None). zone_id is applied to client and node IPv6Address values and therefore to the default route via, but not to the on-link prefix.

IPv6Network has no scope_id. A phone LCI client is multi-homed (Wi-Fi/cellular plus USB/BLE). Installing the oracle table as-is treats all fe80::/10 as on-link with no device, which breaks ND on other interfaces. The oracle has the zone (client.scope_id / node.scope_id) and does not put it on the on-link entry.

Spec 11 section 17.4 table is the product of this function. Zone support was added as local metadata; the routing table is only half-zoned.

## Where

python/src/lichen/client/addressing.py:50-63 LciRoute
python/src/lichen/client/addressing.py:84-89 routing_table
python/src/lichen/client/addressing.py:99-105 static_assignment
design: IPv6Network cannot carry a zone. Add interface/zone on LciRoute, or document and return a scoped on-link entry. Installing unscoped fe80::/10 on a phone (Wi-Fi + USB/BLE LCI) hijacks other link-local interfaces.
acceptance_criteria: When static_assignment or eui64_assignment is given zone_id, routing_table() on-link fe80::/10 is bound to that zone/interface (LciRoute field or equivalent). Default ::/0 via remains the zoned node address. Unzoned assignments stay spec 17.4 unzoned. A multi-interface consumer can install the on-link prefix on the LCI iface only.
